purpose: Investigate which inputs to the existing Lean memory encoder account for the effect of exchanging newest memory between the recent and spread sequence-23 trajectories. This follows selected same-read exchange results and is post-hoc mechanism analysis, not a proposed inference strategy.
scope: Source frames 7,11 and subsequent target reads 8,12 of engineering sequence 3; then source frames 47,50 and corresponding target reads 48,51 of previously inspected, inset-excluded sequence 23. Reproduce the archived recent and spread trajectories with a read-only observer and compare all masks and saved traces; inputs and labels never enter policy selection. No new redetection, inference threshold or confidence rule.
capture: Intercept the active Lean predictor's actual _encode_new_memory input arguments and output only for the fixed source frames. Verify two independent captures for each policy on sequence 3, including exact no-op encoder output and equivalence of the saved target-read newest feature block after the actual bfloat16 storage conversion and float materialization. Then capture both archived sequence-23 trajectories without modifying any model computation and require every mask and trace to match the corresponding previously verified run.
interventions: At the frozen target read retain the recipient's query, conditioning, older memory, insurance, pointer suffix, key counts and native decoder/presence handling. Reuse the exact author _encode_new_memory method to re-encode source-frame inputs under a factorial exchange of image feature pyramid, predicted high-resolution mask logits, and native object-score logits between trajectories; use all eight source combinations, in each recipient direction. Preserve the recipient newest spatial position block, which must match the donor's. Convert encoded features to bfloat16 and back exactly as the predictor storage/read path does. Require the all-recipient and all-donor combinations to reproduce the original newest block and the previous same-read newest swap respectively. Mixes can be off-manifold; log inputs and never feed generated states into later video frames.
verification: Before sequence-23 interventions, independently verify encoder source identities, feature and position geometry, source mask/object inputs and exact quantized target block on two independent seq3 captures per trajectory, run two independent full factorial fixed-read seq3 replays and independently reconstruct encoder outputs, memory tensors, attention and decoder. Repeat the fixed-read sequence-23 diagnostic in two fresh processes and independently verify all tensors, object logits, masks and scores. Freeze predictions before opening labels. Track separate mask-only, object-score-only, mask-plus-object and vision-only effects, full source exchanges and same-state no-op controls.
interpretation: The memory encoder is nonlinear and mixed source image/mask/object inputs can be inconsistent, so effects are conditional counterfactuals, not additive contributions or an inference algorithm. They cannot prove that an online policy, object-score override or feature selector will improve full videos. Frames are selected after inspection; sequence independence is unknown.
